tagline: From the Pocomoke cypress to a barrier island of wild horses.
intro: Up from the Virginia line through Stockton, the byway follows the Pocomoke country north to Snow Hill, crosses to Berlin and comes out on the back bays at Ocean City. Side roads run off to bayfront landings at Public Landing and George's Island Landing. Maryland holds 79 miles of a longer route that runs from Cape May in New Jersey to Cape Henry in Virginia.
Offshore lies Assateague, 37 miles of barrier island. It was joined to Fenwick Island until the hurricane of 1933 cut an inlet south of Ocean City, and the jetties built afterward kept it cut.

moments.title: Snow Hill
moments.text: Founded in 1686 and possibly named for a London street, the county seat stands 16 feet above sea level at the head of navigation on the Pocomoke, where canoes go out among bald cypress.

moments.title: Berlin
moments.text: A main street of old brick that was dressed up as Hale, Maryland, for the 1999 film Runaway Bride, with the Hotel Atlantic as one of the settings.

moments.title: Assateague Island
moments.text: Feral horses roam the dunes in bands of two to twelve, called horses in Maryland and ponies in Virginia, with a fence at the state line to keep the two herds apart.

practical: Visit Maryland asks visitors to stay 40 feet from the wild ponies and never feed them.
